newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW - Malaysia April trade deficit.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Malaysia April trade deficit.

text.p: Malaysia reported a 2.1 billion ringgit monthly trade deficit for April on Friday against a surplus of 1.75 billion ringgit in March. Following are comments from analysts and economists.
FRANKLIN TAN, HEAD OF RESEARCH, Y.K. FUNG SECURITIES

"The trade deficit was somewhat expected as Malaysia bought four Boeing 777s and there were a lot of imports of capital goods, mainly driven by last year's high manufacturing approvals. These (approvals) rose around 30 to 40 percent last year.

"The growth in capital goods imports will continue to rise over the next few months. The question the market is asking is when will exports turn? I think it will be three to six months before we have a turnaround in exports.
"I think the (stock) market will go down to 1,050 (on the benchmark Composite Index) before there is any sign of a rebound."
DILIP RATHA, SENIOR ECONOMIST AT W.I. CARR
"My first thoughts were it's obviously a negative number, but I wouldn't worry about it, because we can't explain March's big surplus, also.
"On a three-month moving average, it will be back to the trend level. Down the road, we can expect some surplus, but from the third quarter onwards, it will depend on the yen.
We are expecting the yen to strengthen in the third quarter so the monthly trade data should go into deficit.
KEVIN CHEW, CHIEF ECONOMIST, CASPIAN SECURITIES

"I think the deficit is at the higher end of market expectations. It's mainly lumpy imports that have driven up the import bill. Imports in April were up 10 percent, so there's abnormal factors there.

"The export side is not helping much. Exports in April were quite weak, showing the first contraction since December. But they have been weak since middle of 1996. But I think expectations are geared to the second half, with strong recovery in the electronics sector. You've got good months and bad months."
QUAH HONG CHYE, STRATEGIST AT MERRILL LYNCH

"Exports seem to be falling a little bit, between one and two percent (from April 1996's 15.97 billion ringgit), which is a little bit of a concern given other countries are showing single-digit growth.
"It shows there's no sign of export recovery. But I think it's part of the monthly volatility, because the item pulling up recovery is electronics and textiles.
"This (trade deficit) number was in the market, so it's not surprising."
DANIEL LIAN, REGIONAL ECONOMIST AT NATWEST MARKETS
"It's an off-trend number and was due to imports of capital goods brought into April.
"I don't know whether this a deliberate move but we should see a surplus in the next two months.
"The deficit should not affect the overall trend. Overall trade numbers in Malaysia still look good. The market still expects Malaysia to register a small trade deficit for the year.
"We are maintaining our projection of a trade deficit of about two billion ringgit for the year."
ANDY TAN, GENERAL MANAGER OF MMS INTERNATIONAL
"The first three months we had pretty good figures so this month looks like a catch-up process with lumpy import items like ships and boats recorded.

"Exports are definitely weaker than expected. We had been expecting some growth in that area. But it would appear that the declines were mostly in commodities and oil earnings. It would be more worrisome if there was a decline in manufactured exports. If you look at Indonesia, it had smaller trade surplus because of softer oil prices.

"You have to also look at the cumulative deficit for the first four months and a 109 million ringgit deficit for January-April looks pretty healthy to me. We shouldn't be unduly alarmed by the picture in April. It is in line with forecasts for the year. MMS is still forecasting a one billion ringgit deficit for all of 1997.
